section_notes.1: Names the Main Street Capital Access Act / Main Street Act and lists eight titles. Header, table of contents and title bridges are retained separately from the numbered operative sections.
section_notes.101: Amends ROAD §908: 180-day to 90-day review; joint discretionary significant-adverse-safety-and-soundness determination only January 1–June 30, 2031. Without that determination the authorities become permanent; with it only qualifying banks insured before the determination retain the grandfathered treatment, with reasons reported publicly and to committees. Eligibility dates change to on/after January 1, 2026. The enacted imported §908 baseline remains unqualified.
section_notes.102: Separate OCC, NCUA, Federal Reserve, FDIC and joint state-charter reporting branches retain their listed application statuses, mean/median requirements and practicability qualifications. State includes DC and territories. Top-tier holding-company treatment excludes control by another holding company; institutional definitions are imported.
section_notes.103: Adds Treasury/designee annual testimony concerning CDFI Fund operations, mentor-protege financial-agent programme and certification/report streamlining; appearance remains at committee chairs’ discretion.
section_notes.104: Distinguishes the sense-of-Congress paragraph from §4713a amendments. Retains outstanding-principal edits, minimum $25 million guarantee, $1 billion fiscal-year total, 10–15 basis-point fee, literal September 30, 2014 → December 31, 2028 substitution, clerical amendment and three-year effectiveness report. No integrated baseline is reconstructed.
section_notes.201: Five regulators include NCUA and CFPB. Regulatory action excludes institution-specific enforcement, adjudication and orders. Post-enactment tailoring considers risk/business model, aggregate and third-party burden, statutory intent and documentation in notices/final actions. Agency reports at one year and annually; GAO at 18 months. Reduced first/third-quarter reports apply only to community-bank-leverage-eligible institutions. Modernization report has its own 18-month clock and state-supervisor consultation.
section_notes.202: Within 180 days, revise 12 CFR part 225 Appendix C to a $6 billion consolidated-asset threshold for bank and savings-and-loan holding companies. Other baseline provisions are not supplied by this reading.
section_notes.203: Inserts Financial Stability Act §§177/178. §177: adjustment after one year then each five years, only a ratio above one; GDP/CPI study and choice within three months; rounding $50 billion at/above $100 billion and $5 billion below; April 5 publication and following January 1 effectiveness. §178: literal June 30, 2026 review then first day of each five-year period, covering §165 and cross-referencing regulations/nonstatutory thresholds; feasible uniformity/rounding and reporting are distinct qualifications. The chronology is not repaired.
section_notes.204: April 1, 2031 then each five years: increase only when the selected GDP/CPI ratio exceeds one; denominator is the calendar year preceding April 1, 2026. Twelve rounding bands run from $50 billion to $0.50. April 5 publication and following January 1 effectiveness differ. Fourteen covered-authority entries and literal paragraph/quotation references remain exact.
section_notes.301: Findings are legislative assertions. New FFIEC §1012 recommendations precede joint rules due 12 months after recommendations, with at least 90 days for comments. BSA/AML/terror-financing compliance and safety-and-soundness/enforcement savings remain. Separate well-managed definition striking operators require the imported baseline; no removed text is guessed.
section_notes.302: Inserts §§1013–1016 and changes definitions, Council costs and judicial-election routes. §1013 excludes continuous/resident examinations; 270-day exam limit allows written-reason extension, final report is 90 days after the later exit/additional-information event, exit within 30 days subject to reasoned extension. §1014 has receipt/missing-information/cure and three distinct determination clocks, requester/fact-specific good-faith reliance, no precedent for others, confidentiality, three revocation grounds, cost-based fees and no final-agency-action status. §1015 board has three classes, separate experience/employment bars, terms/quorum transition, discretion, confidentiality and 1/5 agency assessments. §1016 has information/hearing/record-close clocks, de novo review under policies then in effect, redaction/anti-retaliation/counsel/transcript and enforcement savings; no concurrent board/agency review. Base agency definition has four agencies, CFPB only for §§1012–1015; uninsured credit unions excluded for §§1013–1016. Council 1/4 costs differ from Office 1/5. FDIA and FCUA penalty judicial elections each retain 20-day requests, missed-request consequences, distinct cross-reference lists and saved administrative/consent-order authority. Literal 1014/1013, 30/60-day and redesignation/import issues remain flagged below, not corrected.
section_notes.303: For well-managed/well-capitalized institutions at or below $6 billion, the next exam after a full-scope on-site exam shall be limited-scope as determined by the agency. Upon institutional request, combine two or three otherwise separate safety-and-soundness, consumer-compliance, and information-technology/cybersecurity examinations, as specified by the institution, at the same time. IDI exception includes a formal proceeding/order OR newly acquired control; CU exception is the formal-proceeding/order branch. Twelve-month rules and offsite/targeted/additional-exam savings remain. Separate practices/reports branch uses strictly less than $6 billion and maximum practicability. No blanket exam exemption is supplied.
section_notes.304: Legislative findings are not independently established facts. Own agency and reputational-risk definitions retain the exception for publicity concerning unlawful transactions connected with a designated FTO/state sponsor. Study/determination within one year precedes removal/prohibitions ONLY if removal would not threaten safety and soundness; five categories remain enumerated. The 180-day implementation-report clock is retained separately. INA §219 and state-sponsor authorities concern distinct designation mechanisms, not individual status.
section_notes.401: Replaces FDIC §1812(a)(1)(C) with three PAS US citizens, including separate state-supervision and primarily-under-$17-billion-bank experience requirements. Maximum two appointed terms and 12 total years remain. A dated §1812 baseline is needed before claiming which citizenship/eligibility language is new.
section_notes.402: Post-enactment guidance must carry the specified prominent first-page statement: no independent force of law, no binding rights/obligations, noncompliance not conclusive. Nine-agency list and six exclusions—including APA notice/comment, specified exceptions, adjudication and internal/executive legal advice—are retained. This is not a statutory-law exemption.
section_notes.403: Review interval changes 10 to eight years. Internal cumulative review has seven factors, quantification only to extent practicable, recommendations and agency responses; no automatic repeal. Public-comment and reporting requirements remain. Incorporated new FFIEC §1003 has section-specific CFPB scope that must not be flattened.
section_notes.501: New Federal Reserve §10 paragraph 11 review begins in 60 days and completes within 240, with nine topics. Remediation plan carries milestones/interim controls; 365-day report follows agency feedback, with semiannual testimony and annual Board/IG reports. Confidential annex is conditional on specified material risks. Repeal requires both Congress notification and public website notice that the plan is fully implemented, not a fixed expiry.
section_notes.502: Printed reciprocal-deposit threshold changes $96,333,333,333 to $250 billion. CAMELS 1/2/3 and newly insured/unexamined current-or-prior-calendar-year branches do not replace all other agent-institution criteria. FDIC may waive some/all previously excepted deposits, on application, fixed/indefinite period, only under the negative-safety-and-soundness predicate. Six-month study/report retains 2018-forward period and practicability qualifiers.
section_notes.601: Three competition-consideration lanes (FDIA/BHCA/HOLA): resulting assets below $10 billion AND not the only physical presence in any relevant MSA. Specified monopoly/competition factors differ from all merger criteria. FDIA reporting baseline and forward sequencing with §604(b)/(c) remain explicit.
section_notes.602: GAO study of merger commitments/conditions includes statutory and extrastatutory metrics, benefits/risks, safety/stability/competition/availability; report within one year. Own four-agency definition says NCUA Board; application includes notices/requests, IDI includes insured credit unions. Six imported merger routes are retained.
section_notes.603: Four agency IGs review within one year then every three: mean/median, delay, statutory criteria, impacts and recommendations. Report at conclusion publicly/to committees; agency implementation plan only to extent appropriate. Literal subsection-(a) report reference is retained even though report provision is (b). Own definitions are kept separate from §602.
section_notes.604: Three application lanes retain 30-day completeness/missing-information notice, detailed material-deficiency response and complexity extensions. BHCA says additional period ≤60 days; HOLA/FDIA say period ≤60 days. Third-party material is excluded only for completeness. Decision at 120 days after INITIAL submission regardless of completeness; deemed grant on lapse, applicant-request tolling at most 30 days beyond deadline. Deletes former complete-record 91/90-day clocks. Forward sequencing with §601 is retained.
section_notes.701: FDIC alternative authority is discretionary, subject to clause-(iii) requirements plus joint Federal Reserve/FDIC determination after Treasury consultation. Least-cost non-GSIB alternative must cost no more than liquidation; gap versus covered GSIB alternative must fit rule maximum. Buyer assessment at least five years, case criteria, two one-year rules and 30-day cost report remain distinct. Cost imports and §13(c)(4)(H) nonapplication do not establish any actual resolution outcome.
section_notes.702: Joint study of 2008-forward shelf approvals and 2023 receiverships, entry barriers, benefits/risks/private equity; one-year report. Definitions materially name the FDIC November 26, 2008 press release and OCC October 2017 Cumulative Activities Permissible report. Exact editions are unqualified here. Study questions are not established factual findings.
section_notes.703: Separate default/assistance exceptions from concentration exceptions requiring clear-and-convincing necessity AND no qualified bid. Five statutory lanes and their distinct predicates stay literal. Qualified bid has separate company/affiliate and resulting-IDI capital tests and imported definitions. Joint 30-day waiver report includes alternatives/justification/recommendations and public redaction. New §13(c)(4)(J) excludes listed prohibited bids from least-cost methods; forward §701 sequencing remains. The literal paragraph-(2) prohibition cross-reference is not repaired.
section_notes.801: Merchant-investment holding minimum 15 years. For already-held investments the 15 years run from INITIAL investment, not another 15 years after enactment. Federal Reserve study within one year; report at 18 months, retaining enumerated size/risk/activity/housing/infrastructure factors.
section_notes.802: Separate bank and credit-union partnership studies/reports due in one year; formation, competition, protection, capabilities, funding and possible law/rule/guidance changes are study topics, not approvals. Own banking-organization definition imports §1813.
section_notes.803: Reduces Federal Reserve statutory surplus cap by $425 million, explicitly effective September 1, 2036. Footer records House passage July 21, 2026. No earlier effect is inferred.
